title: Sums of two squares are closed under multiplication (over the constructed integers)
statement: If m and n are each a sum of two integer squares then so is their product. This is the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity read as a closure property of the predicate Int.IsSumOfTwoSquares n := exists a b, n = a*a + b*b, which this lane declared as a named Definition so that the whole two-squares family quantifies over one term instead of four spellings of the same double existential.

formal.statement: theorem Int.isSumOfTwoSquares_mul : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : Int.IsSumOfTwoSquares x0) -> ((x3 : Int.IsSumOfTwoSquares x1) -> Int.IsSumOfTwoSquares (Int.mul x0 x1)))))

evidence.notes: Two independent failure modes, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing: int_theorem_inventory exits non-zero when the named filter matches nothing, and grep -c exits 1 printing 0 when the anchored line is absent. Anchored with [[:space:]] and never with a backslash-t, which a scripted (GNU) grep reads as a literal t. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this tool builds the constructed carriers and overflows the default debug thread stack. The anchor AFTER the name is load-bearing here, because Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci' is a different declaration whose rendered name has Int.brahmaguptaFibonacci as a prefix.

prior_art.what: the composition identity for sums of two squares (Brahmagupta 628, restated by Fibonacci 1225), Fermat's theorem on sums of two squares (asserted 1640) and Euler's descent proof (1749)
prior_art.where: classical number theory; standard textbook material
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary sources

notes: Int.IsSumOfTwoSquares is a DEFINITION, and the trusted gate cannot tell a Definition it is wrong: a function returning the wrong Prop still has type Int -> Prop. So its meaning is settled only by two_squares_tests. 5 = 1^2+2^2, 13 = 2^2+3^2 and 17 = 1^2+4^2 are admitted through the intro rule with Eq.refl as the equation, which means the kernel computes the sum of squares itself; 5 = 1^2+1^2, 13 = 2^2+2^2 and 3 = 1^2+1^2 are refused; and def_eq separates the declared body from an a*b + a*b variant at free variables. One negative control in that file was found VACUOUS on its first honest run -- inner_predicate 17 1 at 4 and its swap both reduce to 17 -- and was moved to free variables.
